_meta.indication: ALECENSA is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have progressed on or are intolerant to crizotinib; approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 1/2 (two-part: dose-finding portion followed by activity-estimating portion at the recommended Phase 2 dose)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multicenter, single-arm, two-part trial with an activity-estimating portion at alectinib 600 mg orally twice daily.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with ALK-positive NSCLC who had disease progression following crizotinib.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (ORR) by independent review committee (IRC).
pivotal_trials.result: ORR by IRC 38% (95% CI 28; 49), 33 responders; median duration of response 7.5 months (95% CI 4.9, NE).

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 1/2 (two-part: dose-finding portion followed by activity-estimating portion at the recommended Phase 2 dose)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multicenter, single-arm, two-part trial with an activity-estimating portion at alectinib 600 mg twice daily.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with ALK-positive NSCLC who had disease progression on or following crizotinib or who were unable to tolerate crizotinib.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Objective response rate (ORR) by independent review committee (IRC).
pivotal_trials.result: ORR by IRC 44% (95% CI 36; 53), 61 responders; median duration of response 11.2 months (95% CI 9.6, NE).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=20%) were fatigue (41%), constipation (34%), edema (30%) and myalgia (29%). Most serious adverse reactions were hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease, muscular toxicity (CPK elevation and severe myalgia), and bradycardia. Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 2.8% of the 253 patients.
target_moa: Alectinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets ALK and RET; it inhibits ALK phosphorylation and ALK-mediated activation of downstream signaling proteins STAT3 and AKT, decreasing tumor cell viability in cell lines harboring ALK fusions, amplifications, or activating mutations.

rems.type: REMS are not required to ensure safe and effective use of alectinib in the indicated patient population; the NDA did not contain proposed REMS.

companion_dx_detail: No named companion diagnostic; ALK rearrangement was required to be confirmed by an FDA-approved test.

advisory_committee.vote: This NDA was not referred to the Oncologics Drug Advisory Committee because it is not the first drug in its class, the safety profile is acceptable, and the application did not raise safety or efficacy issues in the intended population.

description.text: Expanded ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC indication to first-line by removing restriction to patients who progressed on or were intolerant to crizotinib; also converted accelerated approval to full approval

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA expands the approved indication for the treatment of patients with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) as detected by an FDA-approved test by removing the restriction for use only in patients who have progressed on or are intolerant to crizotinib. This approval also fulfills PMR 2995-1 cited in the December 11, 2015 approval letter for NDA 208434.

summary.text: Alectinib received accelerated approval on December 11, 2015 based on durable tumor response rate and duration of response in two single-arm trials, with a required confirmatory randomized trial (Study BO28984). It had Breakthrough Therapy designation (June 26, 2013) and orphan drug designation (January 27, 2015).
